Indicators: census tables and consumer prices

Source: vignettes/census-indicators.Rmd
census-indicators.Rmd
library(knbsdata)

knbs_indicators() lists what every verified indicator source serves, and knbs_get_indicator() returns one indicator as tidy observations. Three families exist today: tables from the 2019 Population and Housing Census (CC BY 4.0), the monthly consumer price series from the KNBS CPI Explorer, the 323 economic dataflows of the KNBS Data Portal — GDP, trade, balance of payments, county government finance and much else, in SDMX form — and the 202 datasets republished by Kenya Open Data for Africa, which carry the one thing no first-party portal serves as data: Gross County Product.

knbs_indicators()                  # all families, source_id says which
cpi <- knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", start = "2020-01")
gdp <- knbs_get_indicator("DF_NAT_GDPCP")
pop <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_level = "county")
gcp <- knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc") # Gross County Product, 2013-2020

The Data Portal (SDMX)

Every dataflow keeps its SDMX id (DF_NAT_GDPCP, DF_BOP_A, DF_CPI_R…); knbs_indicators(source = "knbs_opendata") lists all 323 with their statistical domain as topic. Annual flows carry integer-year periods; monthly and quarterly ones carry first-of-period Dates, so start and end behave as everywhere else. Dimensions vary per flow; each becomes a pair of columns named by its SDMX id in lower case — na_indic holding the labels (“Accommodation and food service activities”) and na_indic_code the codes — and a Sex dimension becomes sex, lower-cased as in the census tables. The ids name the columns, not the portal’s labels, because the portal labels ten different dimensions just “Indicator”. Single-category dimensions (“Prices = Current prices”, “Unit = Kenya Shillings”) are facts about the whole dataflow and fold into knbs_metadata() notes instead of constant columns.

Two cautions: the portal states no licence, and its geography codes are SDMX area codes, not census territories — geo_level is NA there, and they must never be joined against knbs_geographies().

Chunks that contact the services are shown but not run, so building this vignette never depends on them.

Open Data for Africa (the republisher)

knbs_indicators(source = "opendataforafrica") lists the 202 datasets of kenya.opendataforafrica.org, the Knoema-operated portal on KNBS’s own portals page — 169 sourced from KNBS, the rest from the Central Bank of Kenya, ministries and agencies. Dataset ids are the portal’s own opaque slugs, so name search is the natural way in:

knbs_indicators(source = "opendataforafrica", search = "county product")
gcp <- knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc")
gcp[gcp$table_code == "T3" & gcp$period == 2020, ]  # current-price GCP, 2020

Three behaviours to know:

  • Mixed frequencies. One dataset may hold annual, quarterly and monthly series side by side. Annual periods are integer years and sub-annual ones are Dates, which cannot share a column, so a mixed dataset refuses to pick silently — say frequency = "annual" (or "quarterly", "monthly") to choose.
  • Republished provenance. knbs_metadata() names the portal, the original producer, the dataset’s own licence label (most KNBS-sourced datasets state “Public Domain”) and the portal’s publication and update dates — the data vintage is visible, and can lag the producer’s newest PDFs.
  • Geography codes are the portal’s region codes (KE, KE-110-NA, …), geo_level is NA, and they must never be joined against knbs_geographies().

Consumer prices

Three indicators, all monthly, all from one underlying series:

id measure unit
CPI_ALL_ITEMS the index level index points
CPI_INFLATION_YOY year-on-year change percent
CPI_INFLATION_MOM month-on-month change percent

period is a Date at the first of the month, with a period_label like "2026-06". start and end take a year, a "YYYY-MM" month, or a date.

knbs_get_indicator("CPI_INFLATION_YOY", start = 2015, end = 2020)

CPI geography is not census geography

The default is the national series. The other level is "region" — the CPI collection strata: the Nairobi income bands, Nairobi Combined, and Rest of Urban.

knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", geo_level = "region")
knbs_get_indicator("CPI_ALL_ITEMS", geo_code = c("national", "1"))

These region codes are the source’s own and mean nothing outside it. Do not join them against knbs_geographies() — different coding system, different concept, and the package keeps them apart deliberately.

Two more honesty notes, both from the source audit:

  • The region list also names the former provinces (Central, Coast, Eastern, North Eastern, Nyanza, Rift Valley, Western), but they carry no data in any period. Asking for one returns zero rows, because that is the source’s answer.
  • The portal states no licence and does not state the index base period. knbs_metadata() on any result says both, so the caveat travels with the data rather than living only in this vignette.

Retail prices

The same portal publishes the monthly national average retail prices of the 22 commodities tracked for the CPI basket, in Kenya Shillings per stated unit:

knbs_retail_prices(commodity = "petrol", start = 2024)
knbs_retail_prices(start = "2026-06", end = "2026-06")   # one month, all 22

One row per commodity per month: commodity_code (CPI001–CPI022), commodity, unit, quantity, period, price. National only — the source holds no regional retail prices — and the licence caveat above applies here too.

Census tables

What the census source is, and is not

Three properties worth knowing before you use it:

  • It is census data. Every table describes 2019. There are no time series here: period is 2019 throughout, and frequency is NA because a census table is not a recurring release. Consumer prices, GDP and other running indicators are not in this source (see the source-status vignette for where that work stands).
  • It is served over plain HTTP. The API host has no TLS listener, so traffic to it is unencrypted in transit. It carries only public census aggregates and no credentials; the registry records the exception explicitly.
  • It is first-party. The service is operated by KNBS (built with Istat, Italy’s national statistical institute) and linked from KNBS’s own portals page.

Finding a table 

knbs_indicators()
knbs_indicators(topic = "Population")
knbs_indicators(search = "marital")

Thirty-two tables across four populated themes at the time of writing.

Getting observations 

pop <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001")
pop

You can pass a name instead of an id; if several tables match you get an error listing the candidates rather than a silently chosen one.

The result has one row per cell:

  • Core columns: indicator_id, indicator_name, period, value.
  • Geography, where the table has it: geo_code, geo_name, geo_level. Codes keep their leading zeros — "00" is Kenya, two digits are counties, four digits are sub-counties — and geo_level says which ("national", "county", "subcounty").
  • Sex, where the table has it, using the source’s own categories (the 2019 census enumerated intersex as well as female and male).
  • Every other dimension becomes a pair of columns under a short, readable name: marital_status holding the source’s labels (“Never Married”, “Total”) and marital_status_code its codes ("1", "T"). The census API names its dimensions by questionnaire variable (p18_vs1) and labels them in long prose, so the names are curated, one per dimension the 2019 tables carry: age, religion, schooling_status, internet_use, household_head_sex and so on. A dimension added later that has no curated name keeps its source id. The source’s own dimension labels are in knbs_metadata(pop)$notes.
  • Age mixes single years ("0" to "99") with five-year groups ("0-4" … "95-99", "100-120") and a total, so summing every row counts people twice. age_type says which is which — "total", "single_year", "age_group" or "other" — and the groups are checked, on every read, to add up to the total and the single years to their group. filter(age_type == "age_group") gives a population pyramid that adds up.

Filtering geography 

counties <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_level = "county")
nairobi  <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_code = "47")

Filters are applied after retrieval — the API serves whole tables — so the first call and the second cost the same request. Tables are cached for seven days by default.

A worked example

County population aged 12+, both sexes, all marital statuses:

pop <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_level = "county")
totals <- pop[pop$sex == "total" & pop$marital_status == "Total",
              c("geo_code", "geo_name", "value")]
totals[order(-totals$value), ]

Because geo_code is character with leading zeros intact, these codes join cleanly against any other dataset keyed the same way.

Provenance and citation 

knbs_metadata(pop)
knbs_cite(pop)

The metadata carry the licence statement, the release date (2019-12-31), the source statement (“KNBS Population Census 2019”) and the dimension list; the citation is built from them.

Honesty notes

  • unit is NA in the catalogue: the source does not state units, and counts-versus-proportions is knowable only from each table’s name. The package does not guess.
  • An unknown table id is reported as not found. (The API itself answers those requests with HTTP 200 and a body reading errore; the package translates.)
  • The service checks the shape of everything it parses. If the API changes, you get knbs_error_schema_changed, not a plausible-looking wrong table.
